passage: At 6.40 p.m., with the auditors due at ten the next morning, Manoj dropped a file on Dhruv's desk. "The approval note is missing. Just date it last Tuesday. Everyone does it, just this once." Dhruv's heart began to race. Outside the window the traffic hummed; the office had emptied. He could hear how easy it would be to say yes and go home. "Sir, I'm not comfortable dating it earlier than it was signed," he said. His voice sounded thin. "I can attach the note with today's date and a line explaining the delay. I can do that right now." Manoj frowned and said, "That looks bad." Dhruv nodded and, after Manoj left, emailed himself a short record of what was asked and what he offered. Then he started on the explanatory line.

qa.a: The auditors were due at ten the next morning.

qa.q: What was Dhruv feeling when he said he was not comfortable?
qa.a: He was frightened and under pressure, since his heart raced and his voice sounded thin. Even so he said no.

qa.q: What could Dhruv do if Manoj presses him again?
qa.a: He can repeat the proper alternative, keep his email record, and take the matter to a compliance officer or a senior he trusts.

qa.q: How might Manoj see Dhruv's offer?
qa.a: Manoj thinks it "looks bad", so Manoj may be worried about the audit and the delay showing. From Manoj's side, backdating looked like a quick way out.

grounding: A boss asks the protagonist to backdate a document 'just this once'; he says he is not comfortable, offers a proper alternative and keeps a record.
